title: Mecp2 perturbation alters a sparse excitability and membrane-gene module rather than a universal Rett-like transcriptome
exact_observed_result: Mecp2 mRNA itself was not FDR-depleted in any measured class, but four of 22 cell types had FDR-supported downstream rows. The richest 151 TH Prkcd/Grin2c signature included Ache, Fxyd7, L1cam, Cacna1g, Mast1, and Mgat5 down plus Itpr1 and Kcnh5 up; Cacna1g was also FDR-down in 155 MB Glut, and Auts2 was the isolated Pvalb FDR hit.
biological_interpretation: Acute Mecp2 perturbation exposes a sparse cell-type-resolved excitability and membrane module, with Cacna1g and Auts2 as the cleanest markers, rather than a uniform Rett-like expression collapse or a single downstream rescue node.

support.description: The thalamic membrane/ion module is mixed-sign, Cacna1g is recurrently down, and Auts2 is the Pvalb marker.

caveats: No Mecp2 self row reached FDR, so protein engagement must be inferred from downstream expression.
Auts2 recurrence outside Pvalb was nominal only.
The Perturb-seq rows do not measure Rett-like electrophysiology, behavior, or developmental time.

prior_expectation.summary: MECP2 loss causes Rett syndrome and MECP2 is a methyl-DNA/chromatin-binding corepressor; prior mouse work also implicates PV interneurons, but the acute scRNA-seq markers here are sparse.

citations.citation: Amir et al., Nature Genetics, 1999. PMID:10508514.
Boxer et al., Molecular Cell, 2020. PMID:31784358.
